svg.title: Three years of Fukushima treated-water discharge: batches and cumulative volume by fiscal year, tank inventory, and outlet tritium concentration compared with Japan's target and the WHO guideline
svg.text: Three years of Fukushima treated-water discharge — the numbers so far
Started Aug 24, 2023 · FY Apr–Mar · Through batch 22 (Aug 17, 2026) · Batch 23 underway (Aug 31–Sept 18, ~7,800 t)
Batches per fiscal year · cumulative volume (t)
FY2023 · 4 batches
FY2024 · 7 batches
FY2025 · 7 batches
FY2026 · 4 batches*
*FY2026: 4 of 8 planned batches done through batch 22 · dark segment = that year's discharge (~7,800 t per batch)
Tank inventory
~1.24 million t left (Aug 2026)
~1.34 million t at start → −7.6% in 3 yrs
New water keeps forming; drop is small
17 of ~1,000 tanks emptied and dismantled
Discharge planned to 2051 (~30 years)
Tritium at the outlet after dilution (Bq/L) — what to compare it with
WHO drinking water
10,000 (guideline value)
Japan target (below)
Batch 22, actual
167–245 — about 1/6–1/9 of the target, 1/40–1/60 of the WHO guideline
Before dilution ~170,000 Bq/L (batch 22) · 3-km alert level 700 Bq/L, never exceeded since discharge began
Bottom line: outlet within limits, no anomaly in Korean waters → but 92% of the tank water remains and discharge continues
→ Still open: non-tritium nuclides, organically bound tritium (OBT), trust over 30 years — keep counting
Sources: TEPCO treated-water portal & FY2026 plan · Korean government briefing 332 (Aug 19, 2026) · Kyodo News (Aug 2026)
As of Sept 2026 · Volume through batch 22 (Aug 17) · Tanks per Aug 2026 disclosure · WHO figure = drinking-water guideline value
